clue.text: Dispute some rock music parts being recycled?

parts.note: a scrap is a quarrel or fight
metal is a loud, heavy style of rock

explanation.surface: A row breaks out while bits of a rock band's set are reused.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by description: old metal parts sent off to be reprocessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded metal items collected and melted down for reuse are exactly what is sent for recycling.

clue.text: Half the house is ringing me up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top
to ring something is to encircle it, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: taken as written, the outer piece
taken as written, the inner piece

explanation.surface: Someone in one half of a house is phoning the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: IS around ME gives IMES, which is then read upwards. A semi is British shorthand for a semi-detached house, one of a joined pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-detached home shares one wall with its neighbour, forming one of a pair of joined dwellings.

clue.text: Overture not very organised — sort out another way

indicators.note: organising something means putting it into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged
very is abbreviated to its usual single letter, and 'not' tells us to drop it

parts.note: taken as written
V is the standard abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A musical overture is in disarray, so someone must rework it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reroute is to send traffic or goods along a different path, so arranging another way through.

clue.text: Air-kiss, welcoming a popular contemporary followed by bore

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the following letters go inside

parts.note: a peck is a light, quick kiss; this is the outer piece
taken as written
in means fashionable or popular
in also means current or modern
then means next or afterwards

explanation.surface: A social kiss for a trendy acquaintance, then someone tedious turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followed by' looks like a link to the definition, but it supplies letters too, leaving just 'bore' to define.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiresome, irritating person or thing is colloquially called this idiom, matching a tedious bore.

clue.text: Wide-ranging passage from 'Arrivederci, Med' I penned when heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means the letters run upwards, bottom to top
a passage from a text is a run of consecutive letters lifted out of the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, through the middle words and into the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone writes a goodbye to the Mediterranean as they travel home northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic disease spreads widely through a population, so the adjective describes something prevalent and far-reaching.

clue.text: Topless vicar causes offence

indicators.note: without its top, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a parson is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman appearing shirtless scandalises the parish.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal act, so it is a crime or offence.

clue.text: Supermarket perhaps with no parking sign

indicators.note: no means without, so the parking letter is removed

parts.note: a supermarket is an example of a shop
P is the parking sign abbreviation, removed here
W is a standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A supermarket lacks any notice telling drivers where to park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parking sign' reads as one phrase, but 'sign' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to display or indicate it, as a sign or symptom does.

clue.text: Say setter put in sexy clues, finally something to chew on

parts.note: hot means sexually attractive
a setter is, for example, a dog breed

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the last letter of clues

explanation.surface: A compiler slips some racy hints into the puzzle, giving solvers food for thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' invites thoughts of the crossword compiler, but here it is the breed of gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankfurters in rolls are food eaten by biting, plural to match the deliberately loose phrase.

clue.text: Twist broadcast presenting driver's point of view

parts.note: to wind is to twist or coil
to screen a programme is to show or broadcast it

explanation.surface: A plot twist on TV is shown from the perspective of someone at the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist looks out through the front glass panel of the car, so it frames what they see.

clue.text: Drink stain can start to irk

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or blemish
a tin is a can

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of irk

explanation.surface: A spilt drink leaves a mark that begins to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth, an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Family member eats lean dairy product

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a son is a family member; this is the outer piece
to lean is to tilt

explanation.surface: A relative eats lean food from the dairy aisle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lean' pretends to be an adjective about meat or diet; it is the verb meaning slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a strong blue-veined English cheese, and cheese is made from milk.

clue.text: Medical worker, a Latino travelling worldwide?

parts.note: an intern is a junior hospital doctor

indicators.note: travelling things move about, so these letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Latin American trainee doctor working across the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something involving many countries spans the globe, though the question mark admits global reach is a stretch.

clue.text: All the countries with capitals equalling the French one

definitions.text: All the countries with capitals equalling the French one

parts.words: All the countries with capitals equalling the French one
parts.note: surface reading: every nation, each with its capital city; setter's reading: the organisation's capital letters spell the French word for one

explanation.surface: Every nation and its capital city, compared with France's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitals' suggests capital cities, but it means initial letters: UN, which is French for 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The international body founded in 1945 brings together nearly every sovereign state on Earth.

clue.text: Abused rep over crop being in seed

indicators.note: turned over, the word is read the other way round

parts.note: taken as written, then reversed

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written; this is the outer piece
to crop is to cut short

explanation.surface: A sales rep frets about a harvest that is still at the seed stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To be persecuted is to be harassed or ill-treated, often for one's beliefs, so mistreated.

clue.text: Linked with Spain, circle dancing keeps tango thrilling

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so a letter is taken inside
dancers move about the floor, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Tango is the NATO alphabet word for T

explanation.surface: A Spanish dance circle performing the tango is exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tango' fits the dancing scene but is only the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric atmosphere or performance is figuratively charged with excitement, as if by a current.

clue.text: One makes less on paper when one's working

definitions.text: One makes less on paper when one's working

parts.words: One makes less on paper when one's working
parts.note: surface reading: someone whose income looks smaller in the accounts; setter's reading: an object that leaves fewer pencil marks on a page while in use

explanation.surface: Someone earns less on paper while actually in employment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes less' reads like earnings; it means reducing what is written.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber block rubs out pencil marks, so using it leaves less writing on the page.

clue.text: Going through Serengeti, ram is unwavering — a course requiring spirit?

indicators.note: the answer goes through the words, running across them unbroken

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word to the start of the last

explanation.surface: A determined ram crosses the Serengeti on a route that demands courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests courage, but means alcohol: the dessert is soaked in liqueur or rum.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian dessert of coffee-soaked sponge is usually laced with brandy or marsala, a pudding course with alcohol.

clue.text: Articulated components of flight goggles

indicators.note: articulated means spoken clearly, so we want a word heard rather than read

parts.note: a flight is a set of steps, made up of individual steps

explanation.surface: Parts of a pilot's flight goggles are jointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests aircraft and 'goggles' pilots' eyewear; here a flight is a staircase and goggles is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To goggle is to gaze with wide eyes, so goggles and stares are both third-person verbs.

clue.text: Move to secure university that offers lots to pick up

definitions.text: that offers lots to pick up

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside, so a letter goes within

parts.note: an action is a move or step; this is the outer piece
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A campaign to protect a university with many places available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' means items for sale, each numbered for bidding.
explanation.definitionFit: A public sale by bidding offers goods in numbered lots for buyers to acquire.

clue.text: Familiar place name announcing its 'greater peel'?

definitions.meaning: straight reading: a well-known nickname for a city
setter's reading: taken literally, the nickname describes oversized fruit, which naturally has more skin

explanation.surface: A nickname for a town that proclaims a bigger peal of bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peel' sounds like a peal of bells, but the joke is fruit skin: a larger fruit has more of it.
explanation.definitionFit: New York City's famous nickname is a well-known informal name for the place.

clue.text: Wise to be well-mannered — scratching bottom, yours truly gets caught

indicators.note: scratching out the bottom removes the final letter of a down entry

parts.note: polite means courteous
yours truly is the writer, I
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A well-bred person is caught scratching their backside, and it is wise to mind one's manners.
explanation.definitionFit: A politic action is shrewd and judicious, well-judged for the circumstances, so prudent.

clue.text: Little rooster eating spread I will give dog

indicators.note: what is eaten ends up inside, so letters go into the middle

parts.note: a cockerel is a young cock; this is the outer piece
a span is the extent something spreads across
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young rooster pecking at a food spread, which the speaker will feed to the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' suggests butter or jam; it is the noun meaning width or reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocker spaniel is a small breed of gun dog with long ears and silky coat.

clue.text: Rude old boy's missed part of act

indicators.note: something missed is left out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: obscene means offensively rude
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A rude former pupil has missed his part in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s reads as 'has', joining old boy to the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A play's act is divided into shorter sections set in one place, each a scene.

clue.text: Eve's first/last sanctuary?

indicators.note: the name's first and last letters are the same, so either points to that one letter

parts.note: Eve starts and ends with the same letter
a den is a private retreat or refuge

explanation.surface: Where the first woman first found refuge, and where she lost it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the garden was Eve's first home and her last place of safety before the Fall.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Eve lived in the garden paradise until expelled, so it was her original and final refuge.

clue.text: Go slowly and take in banks of Loire

parts.note: to take someone in is to deceive or trick them

indicators.note: a river's banks are its two edges, so the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Loire

explanation.surface: Meander along and see the riverbanks of the Loire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take in' suggests sightseeing; it means fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To trickle is to flow in a thin slow stream, so it means proceed little by little.

clue.text: Fired from editing when drunk

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so these letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor is sacked for working while intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suggests being sacked; it means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire something can mean to set it burning, so fired and ignited both mean lit.

clue.text: Veto daughter, shortly 19, consuming Ecstasy

indicators.note: consuming something takes it inside, so a letter goes into the middle

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
19 across is the city's nickname; abbreviated, the city is NY
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A parent forbids their daughter, soon nineteen, from taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: D and NY are joined, then E goes inside. '19' refers to the answer at 19 across, New York's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto a request is to refuse or reject it, which is to deny it.

clue.text: Politician taking on dealer in intoxicating substances

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a publican runs a pub and sells alcohol

explanation.surface: A politician takes on a drug dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intoxicating substances' suggests drugs, but alcohol counts. A publican is the British name for a pub landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A Republican is a member of the American Republican Party, or one opposing monarchy, so a political figure.
